nodes.name: Ni film electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Pure Ni films were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace onto gold electrodes that were polished with alumina slurries from 5 μm down to 50 nm with 15 min sonication in water after each polish.
nodes.source_text: Films were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s and with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace.

nodes.name: Fe film electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Pure Fe films were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace onto gold electrodes that were polished with alumina slurries from 5 μm down to 50 nm with 15 min sonication in water after each polish.
nodes.source_text: Films were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s and with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe film electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-Fe films containing Ni and/or Fe were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace from electrolyte solutions obtained by dissolving nickel sulfate hexahydrate (≥99.99% trace metals basis) and/or iron sulfate heptahydrate (ACS Reagent ≥99.0%) in ultrapure water (18.2 MΩ) sparged with nitrogen gas for 1 h to prevent oxidation of Fe(II) to Fe(III), with metal concentrations varied between 0 and 0.01 M such that deposition baths with less than 50% Fe contained 0.01 M Ni and varying Fe concentration, and baths with greater than 50% Fe contained 0.01 M Fe and varying Ni concentration, onto gold electrodes (99.95%) sheathed in Teflon leaving exposed surfaces of 4 or 5 mm diameter that were polished with alumina slurries from 5 μm down to 50 nm particle size with 15 min sonication in water after each polish.
nodes.source_text: Electrocatalyst films containing Ni and/or Fe were prepared by electrodeposition onto gold electrodes... Films were electrodeposited galvanostatically with a cathodic current density of 50 μA cm⁻² applied for 1125 s and with nitrogen gas flowing in the headspace.

nodes.name: Ni film aging
nodes.procedure: Aged Ni films were prepared by immersion of as-deposited Ni films, without potential cycling, in 10 M KOH solutions for over 24 h. Immersion was carried out in Teflon or polypropylene cells/containers to minimize contaminants from glassware. Electrochemical and in situ Raman characterization was carried out after the Ni redox peaks and OER currents observed in the cyclic voltammograms were stable, typically 5-10 cycles.
nodes.source_text: Aged Ni films were prepared by immersion of as-deposited Ni films, without potential cycling, in 10 M KOH solutions for over 24 h.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The compositions and quantities of the electrodeposited materials were determined by elemental analysis... On the basis of these measurements, we estimate the thicknesses of Ni–Fe films to be ∼25 and ∼70 nm when deposited on roughened and polished gold substrates, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS determines surface compositions of electrodeposited Ni-Fe films for both as-deposited and polarized under OER conditions (335 mV overpotential in 0.1 M KOH) for 1-2 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface compositions of the electrodeposited Ni-Fe films were determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Both as-deposited Ni-Fe films and films which were polarized under OER conditions (335 mV overpotential in 0.1 M KOH) for 1-2 h were examined.
